title: Gogo Roasted Termites
community: Gogo people of Dodoma and central Tanzania — the termite harvest season
author: Mama Salima
desc: Gogo Roasted Termites — flying termites (kumbikumbi) collected at the beginning of the rainy season, dry-roasted with salt until crunchy and nutty. The annual protein harvest of central Tanzania — sustainable, extraordinarily nutritious, and deeply embedded in Gogo and many other Tanzanian traditions.
longDesc: Termite harvesting at the beginning of the rainy season is one of the most widespread food traditions across Tanzania — practised by the Gogo, Sukuma, Hehe, and many other groups. The flying termites (alates) emerge from their mounds after the first heavy rain, drawn to lights, and are collected in enormous quantities. Roasted with salt, they are crunchy, nutty, and high in protein and fat. This is not an exotic food — it is a completely normal, beloved seasonal harvest food for millions of Tanzanians.
steps: Remove wings from termites (they detach easily — roll between palms).
Heat a heavy dry pan over medium heat.
Add termites. Do not add oil — they contain their own fat.
Dry roast, stirring constantly, for 8—10 minutes until crunchy and golden.
Cool before eating — they crisp further as they cool.
chefTips: Wings must be removed — they make eating unpleasant.
No oil is needed — termites contain 30—40% fat by dry weight.
They should be completely crunchy — soft termites are under-roasted.
commonMistakes: Adding oil — not needed, produces greasy result.
cookingScience: Flying termites contain 35—40% protein and 30—40% fat by dry weight — comparable to meat in protein density. They also contain all essential amino acids, making them a complete protein source. Their fat is primarily unsaturated (oleic acid and linoleic acid). Gram for gram, roasted termites are one of the most nutritionally dense foods available.
sustainabilityTips: Insects require 2,000 times less land per gram of protein than beef and produce 100 times less greenhouse gas. Termites are the most sustainable large-scale protein source available in Tanzania.
storage: Consume same day when fresh. Dried roasted termites keep 1 week in an airtight container.
healthBenefits: Complete protein — all essential amino acids.
Very high in iron and zinc.
The most sustainable animal protein available.
culturalNote: Roasted termites are the seasonal gift that Tanzania's entire central plateau celebrates — when the first rains bring the flying termites, communities gather around lights and mounds to collect them. It is a social occasion as much as a food gathering — the termite harvest brings communities together in the same way that fishing or planting does.
